title: Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery
summary: extend ordinary create-only Docs Import to one exact configured sub-scope collection
content_html:
Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery

Status And Order

Active as SSO-1. This is the first Import-parity delivery for configured sub-scopes and must complete before Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery.

It extends the shipped ordinary staged-source Import workflow. It does not add returned-package recognition or canonical overwrite.

SSO-1 also applies one shared ordinary-Markdown hygiene rule before extending the destination target: after any registered integrated collection recognizer has declined the untouched candidate, a well-formed leading front-matter block is stripped from ordinary Markdown preview and body content without becoming identity, routing, or overwrite metadata. Top-level and sub-scope ordinary Import therefore inherit the same normalization.

Complete Outcome

A local Manage docs_subscope report provides one compact 📥 Import icon beside New and 🔧 Actions.

The control opens the existing Docs Import surface with the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection frozen as its exact destination. Supported ordinary HTML, DOCX, Markdown, text, and one-document Markdown-package sources retain their existing preview, conversion, media, create-only, and result semantics while writing the new document into that configured child collection. Ordinary Markdown front matter is removed before body preview rather than rendered as a heading.

Success runs only the owning sub-scope rebuild and refreshes the mounted report. No parent-scope Index, Recent, search, or selection state is used as an alternative destination.

Exact Target And UI Contract

  • The 📥 button is a sibling report-toolbar control and never enters checkbox selection mode or consumes checked IDs.
  • The management contribution supplies one validated mounted { scope, sub_scope } target. The Import surface displays the configured collection label and does not offer a parent-scope fallback.
  • Public reports expose no Import control, service probe, or management module.
  • Ordinary source discovery and format registration remain shared with top-level Docs Import; a second sub-scope file picker or converter is not introduced.
  • Registered integrated collection recognizers receive untouched staged candidates before ordinary Markdown normalization. SSO-1 does not consume or strip provenance that a later edited-review-source recognizer owns.
  • Activating Import does not infer a target from the displayed detail document, URL text, selected parent, staged filename, or most recently used scope.
  • Cancel applies nothing and returns focus to the same report toolbar control.
  • Success refreshes only the owning report inventory and may display the newly created document through its exact child identity.
  • Failure retains the same frozen collection for retry and never creates the document in the parent scope.

Create Contract

  • Ordinary sub-scope Import remains create-only. The destination allocates a new immutable document identity and uses the same atomic create boundary as top-level ordinary Import.
  • For an unclaimed ordinary Markdown source, a well-formed leading front-matter block is stripped before title/body preview and media scanning. A scalar title may be a fallback when no H1 exists; all other fields are ignored and reported, never applied.
  • Malformed or unterminated apparent front matter produces a clear diagnostic rather than partial stripping. Plain Markdown without front matter is unchanged.
  • Imported title and converted body are mapped through the existing ImportContent and per-document planner. The child collection's flatness, metadata defaults, and allowed fields are validated before writing.
  • A source document never supplies canonical overwrite identity. Existing child IDs, filenames, titles, and links do not create a collision prompt.
  • Media and supported staged dependencies use the existing format adapters and publication plan, confined to destinations valid for the child collection.
  • Multi-file selection retains current ordinary Import sequencing and result semantics; this delivery does not turn ordinary Import into an atomic collection apply.
  • The exact child source root is validated before the write. Success invokes the existing confined sub-scope rebuild owner and does not rebuild parent discovery or public projections.

Ownership

  • The sub-scope management contribution owns the toolbar placement and frozen mounted-collection request.
  • The document-report management host validates that request and hands it to the existing lazy Import controller.
  • The shared Import format registry, preview converters, normalized ImportContent, and per-document create planner retain ordinary source behavior.
  • The shared management target resolver and sub-scope source mutation/rebuild services own exact child confinement and follow-through.
  • The existing Import modal owns focus, busy, retry, result, and cancellation lifecycle.

Boundary

In scope:

  • one report-toolbar Import entry for a validated configured sub-scope;
  • ordinary supported staged-source listing, preview, and create-only apply;
  • shared post-recognizer ordinary-Markdown front-matter stripping for both top-level and sub-scope destinations;
  • exact child source targeting and confined rebuild;
  • report refresh and focused service, module, format, and realistic browser evidence; and
  • reusable scope/sub-scope Import target projection for later registered formats.

Not in scope:

  • returned JSON/JSONL package listing, collision planning, or overwrite;
  • edited Docs Review source-folder recognition;
  • changing ordinary top-level Import behavior beyond the shared front-matter hygiene rule;
  • importing into public reports or unconfigured child directories;
  • checked-ID, displayed-document, title, or URL-derived destinations;
  • hierarchy, move, delete, or cross-collection writes; or
  • all-or-nothing multi-file ordinary Import.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: SSO-1.3 complete. SSO-1 is closed; stop before the separate returned-package Import delivery.

Review rule: complete one phase, record exact evidence, and stop for review before the next phase.

[x] SSO-1.0 — Freeze Exact Destination

  • [x] Add one explicit ordinary-Import adoption contract for a configured sub-scope and validate the mounted { scope, sub_scope } request.
  • [x] Preserve parent-scope requests while rejecting blank, unknown, nested, mismatched, and fallback child targets.

SSO-1.0 implementation and evidence

  • The shared managed-document target owner now accepts only exact collection targets shaped as { scope } or { scope, sub_scope }, resolves the configured parent or one-level child source root, and returns the normalized request target.
  • The ordinary Import management adapter adopts that target before staging or format work. Existing parent requests continue through the shipped workflow; a validated child request is explicitly blocked at this checkpoint so it cannot fall through to the parent-only create path before SSO-1.1.
  • Focused service evidence passed 36 tests across the new Import target contract, the shared managed-target suite, and existing ordinary format imports. It covers parent preservation; valid configured child adoption; blank, unknown, nested, mismatched, and fallback targets; and the no-write child gate.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for the two changed service owners and their two focused test modules. Repository diff whitespace validation also passed.
  • Independent diff review found no second resolver, compatibility alias, staged-source inference, or child-to-parent fallback. SSO-1.1 preview, planning, create, media, response, and rebuild propagation; Markdown front-matter normalization; and all report UI remain intentionally unimplemented.

Checkpoint / review gate: exact destination adoption is ready; do not begin SSO-1.1 without review.

[x] SSO-1.1 — Extend Ordinary Preview And Create

  • [x] Carry the exact child target through staged-source preview, normalized planning, allocated identity, atomic create, and result shaping.
  • [x] Normalize well-formed ordinary Markdown front matter only after registered integrated collection recognizers, preserving create-only identity and unchanged plain-Markdown behavior for scope and sub-scope destinations.
  • [x] Reuse registered format conversion and media planning without adding package or overwrite behavior.

SSO-1.1 implementation and evidence

  • The ordinary staged-source service now carries one resolved collection through preview, planning, allocation, create, response, and activity records. Child creates use the exact configured source root, omit hierarchy metadata, return { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }, and invoke only the confined sub-scope rebuild owner; they do not request parent search updates.
  • Direct and one-document-package Markdown now apply one shared normalization after registered package recognition. A leading front-matter block is removed before preview and media scanning; a scalar title is fallback-only; ignored fields and title decisions are reported; apparent malformed or unterminated blocks fail; and plain Markdown is unchanged. Integrated ImportContent adapters retain their existing canonical-markdown handling.
  • Ordinary HTML, DOCX, text, Markdown, Markdown-package, inline-media, and interactive-asset paths continue through the existing converters and media owners. Child imports reuse the parent scope's configured media publication roots because configured sub-scopes intentionally own documents rather than a second media tree.
  • Focused regression evidence passed 181 tests across ordinary import planning, formats, media, returned-package recognition, review-source normalization, management target adoption, confined rebuild behavior, and the local HTTP service boundary.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for all ten changed source and test modules. Repository diff whitespace validation and the focused sensitive-value scan also passed; scan matches were ordinary internal media_token identifiers.
  • Independent diff review found no child-to-parent fallback, second resolver, source-supplied overwrite identity, returned-package child apply, report control, or selection dependency. SSO-1.2 report wiring and modal lifecycle remain intentionally unimplemented.

Checkpoint / review gate: ordinary preview and create are ready for exact configured child destinations; do not begin SSO-1.2 without review.

[x] SSO-1.2 — Add Report Import

  • [x] Add the 📥 Import icon beside New and 🔧 Actions without entering selection mode.
  • [x] Reuse the shared modal lifecycle and refresh only the mounted sub-scope report after success.

SSO-1.2 implementation and evidence

  • The local management contribution now renders one 📥 Import sibling between New and 🔧 Actions. It consumes only the contribution's validated { scope, sub_scope } collection, remains independent of checkbox selection, and is absent when the management action or local service is unavailable.
  • The existing lazy Import controller and modal lifecycle now accept a fixed child destination and the exact report button as the focus-restoration target. Child mode displays the configured collection label, disables destination and type changes, exposes ordinary files only, preserves the current URL, and restores the existing parent-scope mode on a later global open.
  • Successful child requests carry sub_scope; result rendering and Source use the returned exact { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target. The report bridge rejects a result for another collection, then reuses the mounted report's no-store manifest refresh and exact detail load. It does not request the parent Index, Recent, search, or another report.
  • The focused Import and sub-scope report module smokes passed, including exact request and Source bodies, modal-controller routing, duplicate-open suppression, inactive selection state, and the confined manifest/detail refresh. Adjacent ordinary Import collection and management-create module smokes also passed.
  • Focused service regression evidence passed 13 exact-target and sub-scope Import tests. Explicit JavaScript lint passed for ten changed runtime files; Python lint passed for the two changed smoke modules; repository diff whitespace validation passed.
  • Independent diff review found no public control, returned-package child mode, overwrite path, selected-document or URL-derived destination, parent refresh, or second modal. Representative real Analysis/Tags imports, rich-format acceptance, failure-retry acceptance, and durable documentation closeout remain intentionally deferred to SSO-1.3.

Checkpoint / review gate: report Import wiring and confined refresh are ready; do not begin SSO-1.3 without review.

[x] SSO-1.3 — Verify And Accept

  • [x] Prove exact child confinement, create-only allocation, format parity, parent behavior preservation, failure retry, and confined rebuild with focused fixtures.
  • [x] Import representative Markdown and rich-format documents into Analysis/Tags through the real report control and inspect canonical child sources plus refreshed report output.
  • [x] Update the durable Docs Import and sub-scope management documentation, then rebuild Studio docs and search projections.

SSO-1.3 implementation and evidence

  • A real Analysis/Tags report import created d-20260730-143553-290a71 from staged Markdown whose front matter supplied the existing identity d-20260727-225608-f7402d plus review provenance. Import warned that those fields were ignored, allocated the fresh child identity, created a non-viewable source containing only the canonical front matter and body, and refreshed the Manage report to 249 records. The public manifest correctly omitted the non-viewable result.
  • A temporary semantic-HTML source was then imported through the same real 📥 report control. Its result, URL, Source link, and rendered detail all used exact target analysis/tags/d-20260730-144226-eb5e9d; headings, strong and emphasized text, list structure, and one link round-tripped into canonical Markdown and generated HTML. The exact synthetic document and staged source were removed after inspection, and the report reconciled back to 249 records.
  • The focused browser failure fixture now makes the first child request fail, verifies that the selected source and disabled studio / Tags destination remain in place with no terminal success, and retries successfully. Both requests carry the same sub_scope; parent requests remain unchanged and never acquire a child target.
  • Focused format, media, document-planning, target, front-matter, sub-scope, rebuild, and service evidence passed 95 tests with one intentional skip. The Import multi-selection, Import collection, sub-scope report, and management-create browser modules all passed. Explicit Python lint and repository diff whitespace validation passed.
  • The maintained docs-viewer-smoke profile passed all 25 checks, including source lint, site validation, sub-scope report/create/delete, management and review services, and the public read-only boundary. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/sso-1-3-closeout/summary.md.
  • The durable Docs Import operator guide, Docs Import architecture, and Sub-Scope Index Architecture now describe fixed child destinations, ordinary front-matter normalization, exact result/recovery behavior, and confined report refresh.
  • No real manual DOCX, text, or Markdown-package import, narrow-device review, or full assistive-technology audit is claimed; those format paths are covered by focused service/browser fixtures. Returned packages, overwrite, and edited review-source recognition remain outside SSO-1.

Completion Gate

One ordinary staged source is selected from the Analysis/Tags report, previewed through the existing Docs Import workflow, created under the exact configured child source root with a fresh immutable identity, and reflected by the confined report rebuild without any parent-scope, package, overwrite, public, or checkbox-selection side effect.

Closeout: accepted on 2026-07-30. The completion gate is met; SSO-1.0 through SSO-1.3 and this delivery are complete.
